<Section id="top-facts" type="topFacts" title="Top 20 facts" minutes={15}>

1. AI ⊃ machine learning ⊃ deep learning ⊃ generative AI (Day 1).
2. Machine learning learns patterns from data instead of following hand-written rules (Day 1).
3. A model is the learned function; an algorithm is the procedure that produces it (Day 2).
4. Training fits the model; inference uses it to make predictions (Day 2).
5. Real-time inference serves low-latency requests; batch inference scores large datasets offline (Day 2).
6. Overfitting means low training error but high error on new data (Day 2).
7. Underfitting means the model is too simple to capture the pattern (Day 2).
8. Labelled data enables supervised learning (Day 3).
9. Clustering without labels is unsupervised learning (Day 3).
10. Reinforcement learning learns from rewards and penalties (Day 3).
11. Structured data lives in rows and columns; images, audio and free text are unstructured (Day 3).
12. Neural networks are layers of weighted connections trained by backpropagation (Day 4).
13. Convolutional networks suit images; transformers suit sequences such as text (Day 4).
14. Amazon Rekognition analyses images and video (Day 5).
15. Amazon Comprehend extracts insights from text (Day 5).
16. Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text; Amazon Polly converts text to speech (Day 5).
17. Amazon SageMaker AI covers building, training and deploying custom models (Day 6).
18. MLOps automates the ML lifecycle with repeatable pipelines and monitoring (Day 6).
19. Accuracy can mislead on imbalanced data; check precision, recall and F1 (Day 6).
20. Model drift means production data no longer matches training data, so monitor and retrain (Day 6).

</Section>

<Section id="traps" type="traps" title="Exam traps" minutes={5}>

- **"Deep learning is a separate field from ML"** — no: deep learning is a subset of machine learning.
- **"More training accuracy is always better"** — very high training accuracy with poor test accuracy is overfitting.
- **"Clustering needs labels"** — clustering is unsupervised; labels mean supervised learning.
- **"Batch inference for a chatbot"** — interactive, low-latency use cases need real-time inference.
- **"Accuracy is the best metric"** — on imbalanced data prefer precision, recall or F1.

</Section>
